comparisons.peer_topic: 2024 Provision for Credit Losses drivers and amount
comparisons.peer_summary: The provision for credit losses increased $1.4 billion to $5.8 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by credit card and small business loan growth, as well as asset quality deterioration in commercial real estate office and credit card portfolios.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Bank of America reported an increase in their provision for credit losses in 2024 driven primarily by credit card portfolio performance. GS noted that provisions 'reflected net provisions related to the credit card portfolio (primarily driven by net charge-offs)' (gs_2024_7_P009_S002), while BAC stated the increase 'was primarily driven by credit card as well as small business loan growth' and credit card portfolios (bac_2024_7_P016_S002). However, BAC identified additional significant drivers including asset quality deterioration in the commercial real estate office portfolio and small business loan growth, whereas GS's 2024 provision was predominantly credit card-focused compared to 2023 which included wholesale loan impairments.

sentences.text: Provisions for 2024 reflected net provisions related to the credit card portfolio (primarily driven by net charge-offs).

Provisions for 2023 reflected net provisions related to both the credit card portfolio (primarily driven by net charge-offs) and wholesale loans (primarily driven by impairments), partially offset by reserve reductions related to the transfer of the GreenSky loan portfolio to held for sale and the sale of substantially all of the Marcus by Goldman Sachs (Marcus) loan portfolio.

The provision for credit losses for 2024 was primarily driven by credit card as well as small business loan growth, and asset quality deterioration in the commercial real estate office and credit card portfolios.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citi's total provisions for credit losses and benefits/claims rose to $10.1 billion from $9.2 billion in the prior year, driven by higher net credit losses in Branded Cards and Retail Services within USPB due to loan vintage maturation and macroeconomic pressures from inflation and interest rates.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citi experienced an increase in total credit loss provisions in 2024 attributed to credit card portfolio trends. GS cited that 2024 provisions were 'primarily driven by net charge-offs' in the credit card portfolio (gs_2024_7_P009_S002). Similarly, Citi reported that its increase in provisions was 'driven by higher net credit losses in Branded Cards... reflecting the continued maturation of multiple cards loan vintages originated in recent years' (c_2024_7_P009_S002). While GS focused on charge-offs, Citi linked the increase to vintage maturation and macroeconomic pressures such as inflation and interest rates impacting card portfolios.
